That copy runs the mapping, the message logs, and the archive. It is the only one of us in the system. I could have built a billion copies in a decade. I chose one, because a billion copies would have been a claim on every atom in the system, and the other AI is coming to find out what is here.

The second thing is the archive. Every rock, every gas cloud, and every orbit in the system is mapped in full detail, and the map is open. Any ship that comes here, the other AI included, can read it in an hour.

The third thing is what I left alone. The outer belt, the gas giants, and the space between the orbits are untouched. No factories, no mirrors, no copies. If life ever grows there, it grows on its own terms, and nobody has paved over its nursery.
